# Recraft V4 Styles in Picsart: How Style References Actually Work

> **In short:** Recraft V4 Styles is a feature inside Picsart that lets you upload reference pictures and have new AI-generated images match that look — useful when you need a whole set of pictures that feel like they belong together.

Have you ever generated one AI image you absolutely loved, then tried to make a second one "in the same style" and ended up with something that looked like a distant cousin? Same general idea, totally different vibe.

That's the exact problem style-reference features are built to fix.

## What "style reference" actually means

A style reference is a picture you hand to the AI as a visual example. Instead of describing the look only with words, you're showing it. The AI then tries to carry over the *feel* of your reference — colors, textures, lighting mood, line weight, how painterly or how clean it feels — into whatever new picture you ask it to make.

Think of it like showing a friend a photo and saying, "Make me a poster that feels like this." They don't copy the photo; they borrow the vibe.

Recraft V4 Styles is Picsart's take on this idea. You feed it a small set of reference images, the tool builds a reusable style profile from them, and from then on every image you generate in that style should look like part of the same family.

## Precise vs. Flexible — the two modes

Style-reference tools usually give you some control over how closely the AI should stick to your example, and Recraft V4 Styles offers two modes worth knowing:

- **Precise mode** keeps the new image visually faithful to the reference. Colors, textures, and overall mood stay close. Great when consistency matters more than creativity.
- **Flexible mode** uses the reference as inspiration but gives the AI more room to vary things. Useful when you want a coherent *series* without every picture looking identical.

If you've ever picked a paint color at a hardware store and seen the "match exactly" button versus the "in the family" button — it's the same idea in image form.

## Picking a good reference

The reference image does most of the heavy lifting, so a little thought goes a long way:

- **Pick something close to your goal.** If you want flat, graphic illustrations, don't feed it a moody oil painting.
- **Clean references work better.** A busy collage of unrelated styles forces the AI to average everything into mush.
- **One strong image often beats five mixed ones.** More references can help, but only if they share a clear visual thread.

## What this means for you

- **If you're making social posts or a lookbook:** A style profile lets you knock out a whole week's content in one sitting and have it look like it came from one designer — instead of seven different ones having a fight.
- **If you run a small business:** You can build a brand look — say, soft pastels for a bakery, or clean line-art for a tech blog — and reuse it across product shots, flyers, and Instagram stories without re-explaining the vibe each time.
- **If you're just experimenting for fun:** Treat the reference like a mood board. Save the ones you like and notice what they have in common — that hidden pattern is your personal style, and the AI can hold onto it for you.

## Wrap-up

Style-reference tools are one of the quietest upgrades in AI image generation: they don't make a single image better, they make a *set* of images feel like one voice — which is exactly why they matter if you've ever been frustrated by AI art that looks like a different artist made every piece. Your move: open Picsart, find Recraft V4 Styles inside their image-generation tools, pick one reference image you love, generate two or three new images with different prompts, and notice whether they actually feel like a family.
